text:
Brady Skjei is playing 20 minutes a night for a Nashville team that has won seven straight, and he still hasn't scored. Six assists in 20 games, no goals, 20 shots. For a defenseman who once scored 13 goals in a season with Carolina, that's a quiet start.

The goal drought is mostly luck at low volume: 1.15 expected goals, which defensemen usually turn into one or two. The bigger issue is the five-on-five play. The Predators get 44% of the expected goals with him on, nearly five points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him right at replacement level last season.

He is 32 now, in the third year of the contract he signed in Nashville. The skating is still there: 97th percentile for top speed, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 41% of his entries last season. What we'd watch is the pairing. Adam Wilsby's results are much better than his on the same blue line, and if Nashville keeps winning, the minutes may start to drift toward the guys driving it.
